For engineers who know Azure

AWS and Azure: same ideas, different rules and names

Both clouds give new customers trial credit and offer the same service categories. The differences are in the trial rules, the billing container and the details.

The comparison diagram

Click a row in Service mapping to see what AWS has, what Azure has, what both have and what it means in practice. Click a box in Billing and access boundary to see its match on the other side.

Free credits and what happens when they end

Billing and access boundary

AWS

  • Organization → organizational units (OUs) → accounts → resources.
  • Each account is a hard isolation boundary with its own root user.
  • Identity (IAM, IAM Identity Center) sits beside the accounts, not above them.
  • No mandatory resource-group level: tags or optional Resource Groups do that job.

Azure

  • Entra ID tenant → management groups → subscriptions → resource groups → resources.
  • Subscriptions share the tenant's identity.
  • Every resource must sit in a resource group.
  • Azure Policy assignments inherit down through management groups.
Rough mapping: AWS account ≈ Azure subscription · AWS OUs ≈ Azure management groups (the organization root ≈ the Tenant Root Group) · Service Control Policies ≈ Azure Policy.
